chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a woman whom labor pains affect for days, or for a day, or two days, and she sees yellowish discharge or blood, he said: “She performs salat (prayer) so long as she has not given birth. Then if the pain overwhelms her and a prayer passes her by, and she is unable to perform it because of the pain, then she must make up that prayer after she becomes pure.”

key_terms.الْوَجَعُ: pain that may prevent performance of salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَطْهُرُ: she becomes pure, attaining ritual purity after the state requiring purification
key_terms.دَمًا: blood seen during the pre-delivery period
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up an obligatory act after its time has passed

ai.seo_question: Does a woman in labor stop praying before childbirth if she sees blood or yellow discharge?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman experiencing labor pains before childbirth. Seeing yellowish discharge or blood before delivery does not suspend salat (prayer); however, if pain prevents her from praying, she must perform qada' of that salat (prayer) after attaining taharah (ritual purity).
